Is HomeStars worth it? The honest sum for Canadian contractors.

HomeStars is worth it if you reply fast, quote bigger jobs and track what each won job costs you. It is free to join and you only pay when a homeowner shortlists you, but you pay for the shortlist, not the job. Run the sum below on one month of shortlists and you will know whether to keep going, cut back or put the money into Google instead.

Is HomeStars worth it for contractors?

For some Canadian contractors, yes. HomeStars is the Canadian member of the Angi family, and a strong profile with good reviews does win trust with homeowners. Since early 2025 it has also become much cheaper to try: there is no joining fee and no membership fee for new pros. You only pay a lead fee when a homeowner shortlists you.

Whether it pays comes down to three numbers: what each shortlist costs, how many shortlists turn into jobs, and how much profit a typical job leaves you. Here is the quick version:

  • Usually worth it: you do jobs worth a few thousand dollars or more, you can call back within the hour, and you are newer with few reviews elsewhere.
  • Often not worth it: you mostly do small repairs, you are on the tools all day and reply the next evening, or you are already busy from referrals and Google.
  • Always worth it: the free profile. Reviews there show up when people search your company name, and it costs nothing to keep.

How does HomeStars charge contractors in 2026?

HomeStars' own help pages set out the model plainly. The steps are:

  1. You create a free profile and set the area where you want work.
  2. You browse job leads. Each one shows its lead fee before you respond.
  3. You express interest for free and send the homeowner a short message.
  4. The homeowner shortlists you. You get their verified phone number and the lead fee is charged at this point. This is the only time you pay.

HomeStars says the fee is based on what the homeowner enters, such as surface area, quantity and material, and that it is never changed after you respond. It does not publish a price list. Its fees page says there are no joining fees, membership fees or other costs.

The rule that catches people: you pay for the shortlist, not the job. If the homeowner shortlists you and then hires someone else, goes quiet or shelves the project, you still pay, unless the lead qualifies for a credit (more on that below).

What happened to the HomeStars subscription?

If you read older reviews you will see contractors quoting monthly plans of a few hundred dollars. That was the old subscription model. On 21 January 2025 HomeStars moved existing subscribers to a monthly lead fee credit budget based on their old plan, and its help page says they got 50% extra credit on top. A $100 plan, for example, became $150 a month to spend on leads.

That change set off plenty of angry threads on Toronto forums in 2025. Contractors who were used to a flat fee suddenly saw each lead priced separately, and some felt they were getting fewer jobs for the same money. If you are on a legacy plan, check your account to see exactly what you pay and what credit you get, and decide on the numbers, not on the old habit.

How much does a HomeStars job really cost you?

Forget cost per lead. The number that matters is cost per won job:

Cost per won job = total lead fees ÷ jobs won from HomeStars

Here is a worked example. The fees below are made up to show the sum. Put in your own from your account.

StepExample month
Shortlists10
Average lead fee$40
Total spent$400
Homeowners you reached8
Quotes given6
Jobs won2
Cost per won job$400 ÷ 2 = $200

Now compare $200 with the profit on a typical job, after materials and labour:

  • $6,000 basement or bathroom job at 25% profit: $1,500 profit. Paying $200 to win it is a good deal.
  • $1,200 repair at 30% profit: $360 profit. Paying $200 leaves you $160. Thin, but it may fill a gap in a slow month.
  • $300 call out at 35% profit: $105 profit. You paid $200 to lose $95.

You can also turn the sum around to set a limit before you express interest:

Most you should pay per shortlist = typical job profit × your win rate

If a typical job leaves you $900 and you win one shortlist in five (20%), do not pay more than $180 for a shortlist. If you win one in ten, your limit is $90. Track a full month before you trust your win rate.

What do contractors say about HomeStars?

Reviews on Reddit, Trustpilot and trade Facebook groups are mixed, and they tend to split along the same lines:

  • The complaints: paying for shortlists that never pick up, homeowners who are only collecting prices, fees that feel high for small jobs, and frustration with the 2025 switch away from subscriptions. Trades report lead fees ranging from around $30 to well over $100 for larger jobs, but your fees depend on your trade and the job details.
  • The praise: contractors who reply quickly, have a strong set of reviews and quote larger renovation work tend to say it pays, and that the free profile helps them win work that started somewhere else.

The pattern is the same as with Angi in the USA. Speed and job size decide it. Our guide on whether Angi is worth it covers the American side of the same family.

How do you win more HomeStars jobs?

Every shortlist you do not convert makes the next job more expensive. These habits make the biggest difference:

  1. Only express interest in jobs you want. Wrong area, wrong job size or a vague post? Skip it. Expressing interest is free, but every shortlist costs.
  2. Write a specific first message. Homeowners shortlist people who sound like they read the post.
  3. Call within the hour of a shortlist. The first contractor who calls often gets the visit.
  4. Always send one message through HomeStars as well. You need it if you later ask for a credit.
  5. Make the profile do the selling. Real job photos, clear services, your licence or certification where your trade needs one, and recent reviews.
  6. Follow up quotes. Most lost jobs are not lost on price, they just go quiet. See what to do when a customer ghosts you after a quote.

Message to copy: expressing interest

Hi [name], thanks for posting. I'm [your name] from [business], we do [type of work] in [area] every week. From your photos it looks like [one specific detail]. I can come and take a look on [day] or [day] and give you a written quote the same week. Happy to answer any questions here first.

Text to copy: right after a shortlist

Hi [name], it's [your name] from [business]. Thanks for shortlisting us on HomeStars. I just tried to call. When suits you for a quick chat about the [job]? I can visit [day] morning or [day] afternoon.

Message to copy: asking for a review

Hi [name], thanks again for choosing us for the [job]. If you were happy with the work, a short review on HomeStars or Google would help us a lot: [link]. Thanks, [your name].

Can you get a HomeStars lead fee back?

Sometimes. HomeStars' credit policy, updated for shortlists from 25 July 2026, says you may get a credit when:

  • The homeowner's contact details are wrong or not in service.
  • The homeowner asked for the wrong type of work.
  • You were shortlisted for the same job twice.
  • The person is looking for work, not hiring.

An unreachable homeowner only counts if all of these apply: you contacted them within 48 hours of the shortlist, you sent at least one message through HomeStars, they never replied by phone, email or message, and you ask between 7 and 20 days after the shortlist. Ask on day 5 or day 21 and it is not eligible. Approved credits go on your account as lead fee credit, not back to your card.

Put a reminder in your phone for day 8 on every shortlist that goes quiet. Send the homeowner name, the job number and the reason through the support contact form.

What are the best HomeStars alternatives in Canada?

Thumbtack is US only and Angi's Canadian brand is HomeStars, so the real choices look like this:

OptionHow you payGood for
Google Business ProfileFreeEvery contractor. Calls from Google Maps, usually the best value of all
Google Local Services AdsPer lead, prices shown in your accountTrades that want calls from people who picked them
TrustedProsFlat membership, published at $49 to $89 a month by areaTrades who prefer a fixed monthly cost
BarkPrepaid credits to contact each leadFast responders quoting small to medium jobs
Your own websiteOne build cost plus hostingLeads only you get, that keep coming when you stop paying

Start with the free one. Our Google Business Profile checklist covers every setting that matters, and our guide on whether Local Services Ads are worth it runs the same sum for Google. If you are weighing up a site, see what a website costs in Canada.

The best setup for most Canadian contractors is not either/or. Keep a free HomeStars profile for trust, use paid shortlists only on jobs that pass your limit, and build the channels you own so a bad month on any one platform does not empty your diary.

Quick answers

Common questions.

How much does HomeStars cost for contractors?

New pros pay no joining or membership fee. You pay a lead fee only when a homeowner shortlists you, and the fee is shown before you respond. HomeStars does not publish a price list because each fee depends on the job details.

Do I pay HomeStars if I don't get the job?

Yes, if the homeowner shortlisted you. The fee pays for the shortlist and contact details, not the job. Expressing interest is free, so you control your spend by choosing which jobs to respond to.

Are HomeStars leads shared with other contractors?

Homeowners can hear from several pros about the same job, and HomeStars does not publish how many can be shortlisted. Expect to compete, and win on speed, a specific message and a strong profile.

Is HomeStars the same as Angi or HomeAdvisor?

It is the same family. HomeStars describes itself as part of the Instapro Group and Angi family, with Angi and HomeAdvisor in the USA and HomeStars in Canada.

Is HomeStars better than Google Local Services Ads?

Neither wins for everyone. Run the cost per won job sum for each over the same month. Many contractors find Google brings better value once they have reviews, while HomeStars helps newer businesses get their first jobs.

Should I keep a free HomeStars profile if I stop paying?

Yes. It costs nothing, your reviews stay visible and it often shows up when homeowners search your company name. Just stop expressing interest in new leads.
